clue.text: Railing criminal tries to follow cop around

indicators.note: something criminal is bent or crooked, so the word beside it is twisted into new order
turning around sends the word the other way, last letter first
the scrambled word is told to come after, so it is placed second in the answer

blocks.note: to nab is to cop, i.e. catch or arrest
taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A crook jumps a police officer from behind on a stair railing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cop' is a verb here, as in 'cop it', not a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A banister is the handrail running up the side of a staircase.

clue.text: Rather small men, not quite noble

indicators.note: falling just short means the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small
OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers
a toff is a posh or upper-class person

explanation.surface: Little men who are only nearly aristocrats.
explanation.walkthrough: A toff is British slang for a well-to-do, upper-class person.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adverbs of hedging: 'sort of tired' and 'rather tired' qualify a statement to a moderate degree.

clue.text: Witness cheers up cryptic setter

indicators.note: in a down answer, going up means reading the word from bottom to top
cryptic means puzzling or obscure, so the next word is jumbled

blocks.note: ta is informal British thanks
taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sees the crossword compiler and cheers him up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cryptic setter' looks like a description of Picaroon himself; it is an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: An attester is one who formally vouches for something, as a witness to a signature does.

clue.text: Charge very little cash, which is a boost

blocks.note: to charge a glass is to fill it
1p, a single penny, read with the digit as a letter

explanation.surface: Charging a tiny fee is presented as an encouragement.
explanation.walkthrough: The digit 1 doubles as the letter I, so one penny, written 1p, supplies two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A fillip is a stimulus or encouragement, something that gives a lift.

clue.text: Against holding some light material for art

indicators.note: the outer word holds the other inside it like a pair of hands

blocks.note: con, as in pros and cons, means against
a ray is a small beam of light

explanation.surface: Someone objects to dim lighting on an artist's supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: The cloth hidden in this answer is RAYON.
explanation.definitionFit: A crayon is a stick of coloured wax or chalk used for drawing, a basic art medium.

clue.text: Person who manages to fix one office machine

indicators.note: fixing one thing into another sets it firmly inside

blocks.note: one who copes, i.e. manages
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An office manager is sent to repair the photocopier.
explanation.definitionFit: A copier is the photocopying machine found in most workplaces.

clue.text: Way to fire women dipping into a cash supply

indicators.note: something dipping into a supply goes inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
a till is the cash drawer in a shop
W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: Someone is sacked for stealing from the shop takings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire' suggests dismissal; the definition is the military order 'Fire at will!'. The cloth inside is TWILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Firing at will means shooting whenever you choose, a manner of firing in a military command.

clue.text: Unpleasant look about abstemious character

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

blocks.note: a leer is a nasty or lascivious look
TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol

explanation.surface: A sober person is given a nasty glance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' looks like a person; here it is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Character is another word for a written symbol, such as a single letter.

clue.text: A lot of acid in land's mineral deposits

indicators.note: most but not all, so the last letter goes
one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: a state is a land or country; the possessive gives the letters of the plural
lactic acid, as found in sour milk and tired muscles

explanation.surface: Acid in the ground forms mineral deposits, almost a geology note.
explanation.walkthrough: The acid has to be named: lactic acid, shortened by its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalactites are icicle-like limestone formations hanging from cave roofs, built up from dripping minerals.

clue.text: Dalmatian maybe here, without new medical support

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: Split is a city in Dalmatia, where a Dalmatian might live
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A spotty dog is not given a fresh bandage.
explanation.walkthrough: Dalmatian suggests the dog, but means a person from Dalmatia on the Croatian coast. The cloth inside is LINT.
explanation.definitionFit: A splint is a rigid strip strapped to a broken limb to hold it still.

clue.text: What's found in all other across answers for priests

definitions.text: What's found in all other across answers

blocks.clueFragment: What's found in all other across answers
blocks.note: every other across answer hides a fabric: rayon, twill, lint, and so on
the clergy, named after their clerical dress

explanation.walkthrough: Each across answer conceals a material: RAYON, TWILL, LINT, NET, FELT, CORD, JEAN, REP, MOIRE, DRAB, LACE, LAME.
explanation.definitionFit: The cloth is an idiom for the clergy as a body, from their distinctive garb.

clue.text: Bit of flipping Battenburg finally remaining

indicators.note: only a piece of the following word is wanted
flipping turns the piece over so it reads backwards

blocks.note: the letters inside the word Battenburg

explanation.surface: Someone flips a slice of Battenburg cake and the last piece is left.
explanation.walkthrough: Battenburg is a chequered sponge cake. 'Flipping' could be a mild British curse. The cloth here is NET.
explanation.definitionFit: Nett is what is left after all deductions have been taken, as in nett income.

clue.text: Writer considered clue, then shut up

blocks.note: felt means thought or considered
a tip is a hint or clue
to pen is to shut up an animal in an enclosure

explanation.surface: An author ponders a hint, then falls silent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' suggests a person; it is a pen. 'Shut up' means confine, not be quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: A felt-tip pen is a writing implement with a porous fibre point.

clue.text: Dealing with entry in sports day, ready to broadcast later

indicators.note: the first pieces go inside the last ones

blocks.note: re means regarding or concerning
a record is an entry in a log or register
PE, physical education, is school sport
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: Handling a pupil's entry at the school sports day.
explanation.walkthrough: The joined pair goes between the P and E of PE, with D after. The cloth inside is CORD.
explanation.definitionFit: Pre-recorded material is taped in advance and kept to be aired at a later time.

clue.text: Grasped fighter's grass skirts

indicators.note: to skirt is to go round the edge of something

blocks.note: a reed is a tall grass
Ali's, belonging to the boxer Muhammad Ali

explanation.surface: A boxer's grass skirt, as if Ali were in a hula outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass skirts' reads as a noun phrase; skirts is a verb meaning encircles.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise something is to understand it, just as one grasps an idea.

clue.text: Tired and emotional bride ate nuts

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters go wild

blocks.note: the letters of both words together

explanation.surface: A bride, exhausted and overwrought, eats nuts at the reception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tired and emotional' is a British euphemism, popularised by Private Eye, for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebriated is a rare word for intoxicated, the opposite of inebriated's negative-looking prefix.

clue.text: Get furious with cryptic clue for 'rent'

blocks.note: first meaning: lose one's temper and rage
second meaning: two words that each mean rent, one as hire out, one as tear

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase works as a mini cryptic clue: let (rent out) plus rip (a tear) both give the word rent.
explanation.definitionFit: To let rip is an idiom for unleashing anger without restraint.

clue.text: Program from tech giant, leader in tech

indicators.note: the leader is whatever comes first, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: Apple, the computer company
the opening letter of tech

explanation.surface: Software made by a big technology firm, led by its tech chief.
explanation.definitionFit: An applet is a small application, a little computer program run inside another.

clue.text: Judge Anne Rice a terribly tragic writer

indicators.note: done terribly means badly messed up, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: J is the abbreviation for judge
the three words taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A critic rates the vampire novelist Anne Rice as a dreadful writer of tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: Anne Rice wrote Interview with the Vampire. The cloth inside is JEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Racine was the great seventeenth-century French dramatist of tragedies such as Phèdre.

clue.text: Aussie native not feeling alright, not content

indicators.note: with its contents removed only the outer shell remains

blocks.note: numb means without sensation
the first and last letters of alright

explanation.surface: An Australian who feels unwell and unhappy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aussie native' suggests a person, but it is an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The numbat is a small striped termite-eating marsupial found only in Australia.

clue.text: Make popular finale with understanding of music

blocks.note: the end is the finale
an ear for music is a feel for it

explanation.surface: A musical ending that wins over the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: To endear is to make someone liked or loved by others.

clue.text: Salesman with nothing to reclaim after a default

blocks.note: a rep is a sales representative
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A salesman left penniless sets about clawing back goods after missed payments.
explanation.walkthrough: The cloth inside is REP, a ribbed fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: To repo, short for repossess, is to take back goods when the buyer fails to pay.

clue.text: Magic book forbidding love and anger

blocks.note: grim means stern or forbidding
love is zero in tennis
ire is anger

explanation.surface: A spell book that bans romance and rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forbidding' looks like a verb; it is an adjective. The cloth inside is MOIRE, a watered silk.
explanation.definitionFit: A grimoire is a textbook of spells and magical lore.

clue.text: Pat lady's coat, dressing queen in dull fashion

indicators.note: one word is wrapped around the other like clothing
the coat is the outside layer, so only the outer letters count

blocks.note: to dab is to pat lightly
R for Regina, queen
the first and last letters of lady

explanation.surface: Someone pats a woman's coat as they help the queen dress.
explanation.walkthrough: The cloth inside is DRAB, a dull brown fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Drably means in a colourless, dreary way, the adverb of dull.

clue.text: Put large star in Palladium

indicators.note: the joined pieces are set inside the last

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for large
an ace is a star performer
Pd is the chemical symbol for palladium

explanation.surface: A big star is booked at the London Palladium theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The Palladium is a famous London theatre, but here it is the chemical element. The cloth inside is LACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Placed and put are both past forms meaning set something in position.

clue.text: Comment from Jeremiah in weak part of Bible

blocks.note: lame means feeble or weak
NT is the New Testament

explanation.surface: A remark from the prophet found in a feeble section of scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: The Book of Lamentations is traditionally ascribed to Jeremiah. The cloth inside is LAME, a metallic fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A lament is a mournful expression of grief, as in Jeremiah's Lamentations.
